task_summary: Refactored Project Workspace, Dashboard, and Global CSS to completely eliminate low-contrast text in light mode and enforce 100% text opacity across all components. Defined semantic CSS tokens (--text-primary, --text-secondary, --text-muted, and updated --muted-foreground to #374151), mapped light greys (text-gray-400/500) to high-contrast shades (10.3:1 contrast ratio against white), and verified with 17/17 client test files (81/81 passed), 0 route mismatches, 60/60 agentic validation checks, and 4-way Playwright visual contrast audit in light/dark desktop (1440x900) and mobile (390x844).
lessons_learned: Lesson: Relying on generic utility classes like text-muted-foreground or text-gray-400 without strict contrast tokens leads to subtle accessibility regressions on secondary text elements in light mode.

Lesson learned: Setting text opacity (e.g. opacity-50, opacity-75, /90) on dark or muted text compounds contrast decay, causing text that is nominally #374151 to render at failing contrast ratios (< 3:1). Enforcing explicit 100% opacity on all text elements guarantees calculated contrast ratios match computed CSS colors.

Prevention: Introduce semantic CSS custom properties in :root (--text-primary: #000000, --text-secondary: #374151, --text-muted: #4B5563) and update --muted-foreground so existing UI cards automatically satisfy WCAG AA (4.5:1) and AAA (7.0:1) requirements without manual line-by-line refactoring across hundreds of components.
